142.overview:
A vulnerability has been identified in Node.js, affecting users of the experimental permission model when the --allow-fs-write flag is used.

Node.js Permission Model do not operate on file descriptors, however, operations such as `fs.fchown` or `fs.fchmod` can use a "read-only" file descriptor to change the owner and permissions of a file.

This vulnerability affects all users using the experimental permission model in Node.js 20 and Node.js 21.

Please note that at the time this CVE was issued, the permission model is an experimental feature of Node.js.

143.overview:
The CVE-2024-27980 was identified as an incomplete fix for the BatBadBut vulnerability. This vulnerability arises from improper handling of batch files with all possible extensions on Windows via `child_process.spawn` / `child_process.spawnSync`. A malicious command line argument can inject arbitrary commands and achieve code execution even if the shell option is not enabled.

This vulnerability affects all users of `child_process.spawn` and `child_process.spawnSync` on Windows in all active release lines.

144.overview:
A vulnerability has been identified in Node.js, affecting users of the experimental permission model when the --allow-fs-read flag is used.
This flaw arises from an inadequate permission model that fails to restrict file stats through the `fs.lstat` API. As a result, malicious actors can retrieve stats from files that they do not have explicit read access to.

This vulnerability affects all users using the experimental permission model in Node.js 20 and Node.js 22.

Please note that at the time this CVE was issued, the permission model is an experimental feature of Node.js.

145.description: Bypass network import restriction via data URL
145.overview:
A security flaw in Node.js allows a bypass of network import restrictions.
By embedding non-network imports in data URLs, an attacker can execute arbitrary code, compromising system security.

Verified on various platforms, the vulnerability is mitigated by forbidding data URLs in network imports.

Exploiting this flaw can violate network import security, posing a risk to developers and servers.

146.description: Permission model improperly processes UNC paths
146.overview:
The Permission Model assumes that any path starting with two backslashes \\ has a four-character prefix that can be ignored, which is not always true. This subtle bug leads to vulnerable edge cases.

This vulnerability affects Windows users of the Node.js Permission Model in version v20.x and v22.x

147.description: Worker permission bypass via InternalWorker leak in diagnostics
147.overview:
With the aid of the diagnostics_channel utility, an event can be hooked into whenever a worker thread is created. This is not limited only to workers but also exposes internal workers, where an instance of them can be fetched, and its constructor can be grabbed and reinstated for malicious usage. 

This vulnerability affects Permission Model users (--permission) on Node.js v20, v22, and v23.

148.description: Path traversal by drive name in Windows environment
148.overview:
A vulnerability has been identified in Node.js, specifically affecting the handling of drive names in the Windows environment. Certain Node.js functions do not treat drive names as special on Windows. As a result, although Node.js assumes a relative path, it actually refers to the root directory.

On Windows, a path that does not start with the file separator is treated as relative to the current directory. 

This vulnerability affects Windows users of `path.join` API.

149.description: GOAWAY HTTP/2 frames cause memory leak outside heap
149.overview:
A memory leak could occur when a remote peer abruptly closes the socket without sending a GOAWAY notification. Additionally, if an invalid header was detected by nghttp2, causing the connection to be terminated by the peer, the same leak was triggered. This flaw could lead to increased memory consumption and potential denial of service under certain conditions.

This vulnerability affects HTTP/2 Server users on Node.js v18.x, v20.x, v22.x and v23.x.

151.description: Corrupted pointer in node::fs::ReadFileUtf8(const FunctionCallbackInfo<Value>& args) when args[0] is a string.
151.overview:
In Node.js, the `ReadFileUtf8` internal binding leaks memory due to a corrupted pointer in `uv_fs_s.file`: a UTF-16 path buffer is allocated but subsequently overwritten when the file descriptor is set. This results in an unrecoverable memory leak on every call. Repeated use can cause unbounded memory growth, leading to a denial of service.

Impact:
* This vulnerability affects APIs relying on `ReadFileUtf8` on Node.js release lines: v20 and v22.

152.description: Improper error handling in async cryptographic operations crashes process
152.overview: The C++ method SignTraits::DeriveBits() may incorrectly call ThrowException() based on user-supplied inputs when executing in a background thread, crashing the Node.js process. Such cryptographic operations are commonly applied to untrusted inputs. Thus, this mechanism potentially allows an adversary to remotely crash a Node.js runtime.

154.description: Windows Device Names (CON, PRN, AUX) Bypass Path Traversal Protection in path.normalize()
154.overview:
An incomplete fix has been identified for CVE-2025-23084 in Node.js, specifically affecting Windows device names like CON, PRN, and AUX. 

This vulnerability affects Windows users of `path.join` API.

155.overview:
The V8 release used in Node.js v24.0.0 has changed how string hashes are computed using rapidhash. This implementation re-introduces the HashDoS vulnerability as an attacker who can control the strings to be hashed can generate many hash collisions - an attacker can generate collisions even without knowing the hash-seed.

* This vulnerability affects Node.js v24.x users.

156.overview:
A flaw in Node.js’s Permissions model allows attackers to bypass `--allow-fs-read` and `--allow-fs-write` restrictions using crafted relative symlink paths. By chaining directories and symlinks, a script granted access only to the current directory can escape the allowed path and read sensitive files. This breaks the expected isolation guarantees and enables arbitrary file read/write, leading to potential system compromise.
This vulnerability affects users of the permission model on Node.js v20,  v22,  v24, and v25.

157.description: Timeout-based race conditions make Uint8Array/Buffer.alloc non-zerofilled
157.overview: A flaw in Node.js's buffer allocation logic can expose uninitialized memory when allocations are interrupted, when using the `vm` module with the timeout option. Under specific timing conditions, buffers allocated with `Buffer.alloc` and other `TypedArray` instances like `Uint8Array` may contain leftover data from previous operations, allowing in-process secrets like tokens or passwords to leak or causing data corruption. While exploitation typically requires precise timing or in-process code execution, it can become remotely exploitable when untrusted input influences workload and timeouts, leading to potential confidentiality and integrity impact.

158.overview: A flaw in Node.js's permission model allows a file's access and modification timestamps to be changed via `futimes()` even when the process has only read permissions. Unlike `utimes()`, `futimes()` does not apply the expected write-permission checks, which means file metadata can be modified in read-only directories. This behavior could be used to alter timestamps in ways that obscure activity, reducing the reliability of logs. This vulnerability affects users of the permission model on Node.js v20,  v22,  v24, and v25.

159.description: Memory leak that enables remote Denial of Service against applications processing TLS client certificates
159.overview: A memory leak in Node.js’s OpenSSL integration occurs when converting `X.509` certificate fields to UTF-8 without freeing the allocated buffer. When applications call `socket.getPeerCertificate(true)`, each certificate field leaks memory, allowing remote clients to trigger steady memory growth through repeated TLS connections. Over time this can lead to resource exhaustion and denial of service.

160.description: Node.js HTTP/2 server crashes with unhandled error when receiving malformed HEADERS frame

161.description: Uncatchable "Maximum call stack size exceeded" error on Node.js via async_hooks leads to process crashes bypassing error handlers
161.overview: We have identified a bug in Node.js error handling where "Maximum call stack size exceeded" errors become uncatchable when `async_hooks.createHook()` is enabled. Instead of reaching `process.on('uncaughtException')`, the process terminates, making the crash unrecoverable. Applications that rely on `AsyncLocalStorage` (v22, v20) or `async_hooks.createHook()` (v24, v22, v20) become vulnerable to denial-of-service crashes triggered by deep recursion under specific conditions.

163.description: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-21637: loadSNI() in _tls_wrap.js lacks try/catch leading to Remote DoS
163.overview:
A flaw in Node.js TLS error handling leaves `SNICallback` invocations unprotected against synchronous exceptions, while the equivalent ALPN and PSK callbacks were already addressed in CVE-2026-21637. This represents an incomplete fix of that prior vulnerability.

When an `SNICallback` throws synchronously on unexpected input the exception bypasses TLS error handlers and propagates as an uncaught exception, crashing the Node.js process.

* This vulnerability affects all Node.js versions that received the CVE-2026-21637 fix, including **20.x, 22.x, 24.x, and 25.x**, on any TLS server where `SNICallback` may throw on unexpected `servername` input.

164.description: Denial of Service via `__proto__` header name in `req.headersDistinct` (Uncaught `TypeError` crashes Node.js process)
164.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP request handling causes an uncaught `TypeError` when a request is received with a header named `__proto__` and the application accesses `req.headersDistinct`.

When this occurs, `dest["__proto__"]` resolves to `Object.prototype` rather than `undefined`, causing `.push()` to be called on a non-array. This exception is thrown synchronously inside a property getter and cannot be intercepted by `error` event listeners, meaning it cannot be handled without wrapping every `req.headersDistinct` access in a `try/catch`.

* This vulnerability affects all Node.js HTTP servers on **20.x, 22.x, 24.x, and v25.x**

166.description: Assertion error in node_url.cc via malformed URL format leads to Node.js crash
166.overview:
A flaw in Node.js URL processing causes an assertion failure in native code when `url.format()` is called with a malformed internationalized domain name (IDN) containing invalid characters, crashing the Node.js process.

* This vulnerability affects **24.x and 25.x**.

167.description: Timing side-channel in HMAC verification via memcmp() in crypto_hmac.cc leads to potential MAC forgery
167.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HMAC verification uses a non-constant-time comparison when validating user-provided signatures, potentially leaking timing information proportional to the number of matching bytes. Under certain threat models where high-resolution timing measurements are possible, this behavior could be exploited as a timing oracle to infer HMAC values.

Node.js already provides timing-safe comparison primitives used elsewhere in the codebase, indicating this is an oversight rather than an intentional design decision.

This vulnerability affects **20.x, 22.x, 24.x, and 25.x**.

168.description: Memory leak in Node.js HTTP/2 server via WINDOW_UPDATE on stream 0 leads to resource exhaustion
168.overview:
A memory leak occurs in Node.js HTTP/2 servers when a client sends WINDOW_UPDATE frames on stream 0 (connection-level) that cause the flow control window to exceed the maximum value of 2³¹-1. The server correctly sends a GOAWAY frame, but the Http2Session object is never cleaned up.

This vulnerability affects HTTP2 users on Node.js 20, 22, 24 and 25.

169.description: Permission Model Bypass in realpathSync.native Allows File Existence Disclosure
169.overview:
A flaw in Node.js Permission Model filesystem enforcement leaves `fs.realpathSync.native()` without the required read permission checks, while all comparable filesystem functions correctly enforce them.

As a result, code running under `--permission` with restricted `--allow-fs-read` can still use `fs.realpathSync.native()` to check file existence, resolve symlink targets, and enumerate filesystem paths outside of permitted directories.

This vulnerability affects **20.x, 22.x, 24.x, and 25.x** processes using the Permission Model where `--allow-fs-read` is intentionally restricted.

170.overview:
An incomplete fix for CVE-2024-36137 leaves `FileHandle.chmod()` and `FileHandle.chown()` in the promises API without the required permission checks, while their callback-based equivalents (`fs.fchmod()`, `fs.fchown()`) were correctly patched.

As a result, code running under `--permission` with restricted `--allow-fs-write` can still use promise-based `FileHandle` methods to modify file permissions and ownership on already-open file descriptors, bypassing the intended write restrictions.

This vulnerability affects **20.x, 22.x, 24.x, and 25.x** processes using the Permission Model where `--allow-fs-write` is intentionally restricted.

171.overview:
A flaw in V8's string hashing mechanism causes integer-like strings to be hashed to their numeric value, making hash collisions trivially predictable. By crafting a request that causes many such collisions in V8's internal string table, an attacker can significantly degrade performance of the Node.js process.

The most common trigger is any endpoint that calls `JSON.parse()` on attacker-controlled input, as JSON parsing automatically internalizes short strings into the affected hash table.

This vulnerability affects **20.x, 22.x, 24.x, and 25.x**.

172.description: Proxy credentials leaked in ERR_PROXY_TUNNEL error message
172.overview:
A flaw in Node.js proxy tunnel error handling could expose proxy credentials in `ERR_PROXY_TUNNEL` error messages.

When proxy credentials are embedded in the proxy URL, they may be exposed through error handling paths and captured by logs, diagnostics, or other error consumers.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

173.description: Permission Model Bypass via `process.report.writeReport()` Path Misvalidation
173.overview:
A flaw in Node.js Permission Model enforcement allows Bypass via `process.report.writeReport()` Path Misvalidation.

This can lead to confidentiality impact or bypass of the intended security boundary under affected configurations.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

174.description: Node.js unicode dot separator handling can lead to tls wildcard-depth authentication bypass due to resolver and verifier hostname normalization mismat
174.overview:
A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname handling can cause Node.js unicode dot separator handling can lead to tls wildcard-depth authentication bypass due to resolver and verifier hostname normalization mismat.

This can lead to confidentiality impact or bypass of the intended security boundary under affected configurations.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

175.description: Unbounded memory growth in `node:http2` clients via attacker-controlled ORIGIN frames
175.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP/2 client allows a server to send an unlimited number of ORIGIN frames, which could lead to an Out of Memory error on the client.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

176.description: HTTP/2 sessions never clean up after GOAWAY on invalid protocol errors
176.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP/2 server API can cause servers to keep accepting data even after sending a `GOAWAY` frame.

This vulnerability affects two supported release lines: **Node.js 22** and **Node.js 24**.

177.description: Uppercase sni context matching can lead to mtls authorization bypass due to case-sensitive hostname matching
177.overview:
A inconsistency in Node.js hostname matching can cause a trust-policy bypass in multi-context mTLS setups.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

178.description: Embedded-nul hostnames can lead to silent authority rebinding due to c-string truncation in resolver bindings
178.overview:
A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname handling can cause Embedded-nul hostnames can lead to silent authority rebinding due to c-string truncation in resolver bindings.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

179.description: TLS host identity verification bypass via session reuse with different servername leads to unauthorized connections
179.overview:
A flaw in Node.js TLS host verification can cause an attacker to bypass certification validation.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

180.description: Permission Model bypass via FileHandle.utimes() in the promises API
180.overview:
A flaw in Node.js Permission API can cause a file metadata to be modified even on a path that was set as read-only with e.g. `--allow-fs-read`.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

181.description: Unix domain socket server bypasses --permission network restrictions (incomplete CVE-2026-21636 fix)
181.overview:
A flaw in Node.js Permission API can cause a local server to be started (via a Unix domain socket), even without the `--allow-net` permission.

This vulnerability affects one supported release line: **Node.js 26**.

182.description: HTTP Response Queue Poisoning via TOCTOU Race Condition in `http.Agent`
182.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP Agent can cause a client to accept as valid a response that is send before the client has sent the request.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

183.description: Node.js WebCrypto AES Integer Overflow Leads to Remote Process Abort (DoS)
183.overview:
A flaw in Node.js WebCrypto implementation can crash the process if the input of `subtle.encrypt()` is a multiple of 2GiB.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

184.description: HTTP/2 retained header blocks evade maxSessionMemory and enable remote memory exhaustion
184.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP/2 handling can cause HTTP/2 retained header blocks evade maxSessionMemory and enable remote memory exhaustion.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **24.x** and **22.x**.

185.description: Permission Model Bypass: `trace_events.createTracing().enable()` Writes Trace Logs Outside `--allow-fs-write`
185.overview:
A flaw in Node.js Permission Model enforcement allows `trace_events.createTracing().enable()` Writes Trace Logs Outside `--allow-fs-write`.

This can lead to confidentiality impact or bypass of the intended security boundary under affected configurations.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **22.x**, **24.x**, and **26.x**.

186.description: Re-entrant `nghttp2_session_mem_send()` during `nghttp2_session_mem_recv()` causes heap-use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2
186.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP/2 handling allows `nghttp2_session_mem_send()` to be called re-entrantly while `nghttp2_session_mem_recv()` is executing, resulting in a heap-use-after-free.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

187.description: HTTPS Agent PFX object-array key collision allows mTLS client identity reuse across different per-request certificates
187.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HTTPS Agent connection reuse can cause PFX object-array key collisions, allowing mutual TLS (mTLS) client identities to be reused across requests configured with different client certificates.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

188.description: Permission Model bypass: process.report writes (and overwrites) files outside --allow-fs-write paths
188.overview:
A flaw in Node.js Permission Model enforcement allows process.report writes (and overwrites) files outside --allow-fs-write paths.

This can lead to confidentiality impact or bypass of the intended security boundary under affected configurations.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **22.x**, **24.x**, and **26.x**.

189.description: HTTPS Agent TLS session reuse skips hostname verification across identity policies (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48934)
189.overview:
An incomplete fix has been identified in Node.js: HTTPS Agent TLS session reuse skips hostname verification across identity policies (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48934).

This vulnerability affects Node.js **22.x**, **24.x**, and **26.x**.

190.description: node:sqlite SQLTagStore Iterator Replay Lets Attacker Re-Execute Victim-Bound Writes Indefinitely
190.overview:
A flaw in Node.js node:sqlite allows a stale StatementSyncIterator created through DatabaseSync#createTagStore() to continue executing a cached prepared statement after it has been reset and rebound with new parameters. SQLTagStore resets cached statements using sqlite3_reset() directly, bypassing the iterator invalidation mechanism introduced for StatementSync in recent releases

This vulnerability affects Node.js **22.x**, **24.x**, and **26.x**.

191.description: dns.resolveAny() Aborts the Node.js Process When a DNS Response Contains More Than 256 A Records
191.overview:
A flaw in Node.js can cause dns.resolveAny() Aborts the Node.js Process When a DNS Response Contains More Than 256 A Records.

Repeated triggering of this condition can lead to denial of service.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

192.overview:
A flaw in Node.js Permission Model enforcement can over-grant filesystem access across radix-tree prefix boundaries.

Under `--permission`, an attacker who is granted access to one path can abuse boundary handling to read from or write to paths outside the intended filesystem allowlist.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **main**, **22.x**, **24.x**, and **26.x**.

193.description: HTTP Request Smuggling via Silent Header Truncation in Node.js HTTP Parser
193.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP client can cause a request desynchronization for Node.js-based forwarding proxies that rebuild outbound headers from the visible `IncomingMessage` headers while piping the original body to a reused backend connection.

Node.js can omit headers beyond `maxHeadersCount` / `maxHeaderPairs` from `req.headers`, `req.rawHeaders`, and `req.headersDistinct`, while still using those omitted headers internally for HTTP message framing. In particular, `Content-Length` can be hidden from userland while the request body is still delivered.

This vulnerability affects all supported release lines: **Node.js 22**, **Node.js 24**, and **Node.js 26**.

194.description: Reachable assertion in node:zlib sync API crashes the entire process via spoofed TypedArray byteLength (all 11 *Sync functions affected)
194.overview:
A flaw in Node.js allows a spoofed `TypedArray` `byteLength` to trigger a reachable assertion in the synchronous `node:zlib` APIs, causing the entire process to crash. All 11 synchronous zlib functions are affected.

Repeated exploitation of this condition can result in a denial of service.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **22.x**, **24.x**, and **26.x**.

195.description: Keep-alive socket process a response that was written before the request was sent
195.overview:
A flaw in Node.js HTTP Agent connection reuse can cause a client to accept as valid a response that was sent before the client has sent the request. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48931.

The guard that destroys idle keep-alive sockets when unexpected data arrives only runs when the event loop polls for I/O. If an unsolicited response has already reached the socket but has not been read yet when the socket is handed to a new request, for example because the event loop was busy with synchronous work, the guard is removed without seeing it and the data is parsed as the response to the new request.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

196.description: dns.resolve truncates names containing NUL char
196.overview:
A flaw in Node.js DNS resolution allows hostnames containing a NUL byte to be silently truncated by the `dns.resolve*()` functions and `dns.reverse()`. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48930, which only covered `dns.lookup()` and the `net`/`tls` host options.

Because the name is passed to c-ares as a C string, resolving `attacker.example\0.trusted.example` queries `attacker.example` and returns its records without any error. Applications that validate a hostname, for example against a domain allowlist, and then resolve it with `dns.resolve*()` can act on records for a different name than the one they validated.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

197.description: TLS certificate hostname bypass when the IP is written fullwidth digits
197.overview:
A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification allows a certificate without a matching IP address SAN to authenticate a connection to an IPv4 address when the host is written with non-ASCII characters, such as fullwidth digits (`１２７.0.0.1`).

`tls.checkServerIdentity()` did not recognize such hosts as IP addresses, even though they normalize and resolve to a regular IPv4 address, and matched them against the certificate DNS names and Common Name instead. A certificate containing `DNS:127.0.0.1` or `DNS:*.0.0.1` could therefore be accepted for an IP endpoint it was not issued for. This is a regression introduced after the fix for CVE-2026-48618.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x** and **24.x**.

198.description: TLS certificate hostname bypass when the host loosely resolves to an IP address
198.overview:
A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification can cause a server certificate to be validated against a different IP address than the one the client connected to, when the host is a non-canonical IPv4 literal with a leading zero, such as `0127.0.0.1`.

`tls.checkServerIdentity()` normalizes the host following the WHATWG URL rules, which read a leading-zero octet as octal (`0127.0.0.1` becomes `87.0.0.1`), while the connection is made through the operating system resolver, which on some platforms such as macOS reads it as decimal (`127.0.0.1`). A server at the connected address can then be authenticated with a certificate issued for another IP address.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

199.description: Node.js ZipFile returns attacker-controlled prefix bytes after failed ZIP header validation
199.overview:
A flaw in the Node.js `zlib.ZipFile` API can cause it to return bytes that do not belong to the requested entry after the local and central header validation fails.

When `zipEntry.modified` is read on an archive whose local header does not match its central directory, either directly or while compacting the archive, the validation error is caught but the parsed local header is left cached without a content offset. A later content read then returns attacker-controlled bytes from the start of the file instead of rejecting the archive, and CRC-32 verification still passes because the attacker controls the central directory CRC. A Node.js-based scanner can therefore approve different content from what another ZIP implementation extracts from the same archive.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**.

200.description: Permission Model filesystem over-grant via wildcard radix lookup
200.overview: A Node.js Permission Model filesystem over-grant lets a wildcard `--allow-fs-read` or `--allow-fs-write` rule match paths it should not. When the requested path is shorter than the prefix of a wildcard grant, the radix tree lookup stops comparing early and treats the path as a match, so for example `--allow-fs-read=/etc/passwd.*` also allows reading `/etc/passwd`. It requires the wildcard grant to sit directly under the root of the permission tree, such as when it is the only grant for that scope. This is a different root cause from CVE-2026-58043. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

201.description: Improper certificate validation for non-canonical IPv4 hostnames allows DNS SANs to authenticate IP endpoints
201.overview:
A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification allows a certificate with only a DNS SAN to authenticate an IP endpoint when the client connects using a non-canonical IPv4 spelling, such as `0177.0.0.1`, `0x7f.0.0.1`, `2130706433` or `127.1`.

`tls.checkServerIdentity()` did not classify these hosts as IP addresses, but normalized them to their canonical form and matched the result against the certificate DNS names. A certificate containing `DNS:127.0.0.1` and no `IP Address:127.0.0.1` SAN was therefore accepted, while the same certificate is correctly rejected for `127.0.0.1`. Exploitation requires a certificate with a numeric DNS SAN issued by a CA trusted by the client, and a platform resolver that accepts these spellings, such as glibc.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

202.overview:
A flaw in Node.js Permission Model filesystem enforcement leaves `fs.realpathSync()` without the required read permission checks. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-21715, which only covered `fs.realpathSync.native()`.

As a result, code running under `--permission` with restricted `--allow-fs-read` can still use `fs.realpathSync()` to check file existence, resolve symlink targets, and enumerate filesystem paths outside of permitted directories.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

203.description: crypto.randomUUID() and randomInt() entropy caches are saved into user-land startup snapshots and SEAs, so every process repeats the same values
203.overview:
A flaw in Node.js `crypto` causes the internal entropy caches used by `crypto.randomUUID()`, `crypto.randomUUIDv7()`, and `crypto.randomInt()` to be saved into user-land startup snapshots (`--build-snapshot`) and single executable applications built with `useSnapshot`.

If any of these functions, or an API that relies on them such as `URL.createObjectURL()`, is called while the snapshot is built, every process started from that snapshot returns the same values until the cache is refilled: up to 127 UUIDs and about 1,000 `randomInt()` values. Identifiers expected to be unique can collide across processes, and values issued by one process can be predicted by observing another.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

204.description: Node.js Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write permits remote code execution
204.overview:
A flaw in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js allows malformed compressed input to write past the end of an internal decoder buffer.

An invalid block switch was reported as a temporary need for more input instead of a permanent format error, so the streaming decoder kept appending input bytes to an eight-byte internal buffer. An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with `node:zlib` can corrupt process memory, which can lead to a crash, disclosure of process memory, or remote code execution.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

205.description: Remote unauthenticated HTTP/2 heap-buffer-overflow in session.altsvc() with a long origin - github.com/nodejs/node
205.overview: A one-byte heap buffer overflow in Node.js HTTP/2 Alt-Svc handling lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt process memory. When an application passes an attacker-controlled value such as a request's `:authority` header to `Http2Session.altsvc()`, the AltSvc implementation in `src/node_http2.cc` allocates a buffer sized to the origin length and then writes it with a null terminator, placing one byte past the end of the allocation. A single request carrying a long but syntactically valid `:authority` triggers the out-of-bounds write, which aborts the process and serves as a remote heap-corruption primitive. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

206.description: Permission Model Bypass in recursive fs.watch Leaks Names of Denied Descendants
206.overview: A Permission Model bypass in Node.js recursive file watching discloses the names of files and directories the process is not permitted to read. On macOS and Windows, `fs.watch()` and `fs.promises.watch()` in recursive mode are backed by the native `libuv` watcher: `FSEventWrap::Start` checks `kFileSystemRead` only once, on the watched root, and `FSEventWrap::OnEvent` then forwards every filename `libuv` reports (relative paths at any depth) to the JavaScript callback without checking that each path is covered by the read grant. Code running under `--permission` with an exact read grant on a directory can therefore learn names such as `sub/secret.txt` even though `readdir` on that subdirectory is denied. The flaw exposes names and timing metadata, not file contents, and requires macOS or Windows plus files created under the watched directory by another actor. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

207.description: zlib: a pending `params()` plus `destroy()` throws an uncatchable `ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION`
207.overview: An uncatchable exception in the Node.js zlib streaming API lets a peer crash a process by disconnecting while data is being compressed. `zlib.params()` queues a flush and completes its work in that write's callback; if the stream is destroyed first, as `pipeline()` does when the peer goes away, `Writable` still invokes the callback with an error, but the callback ignores its arguments and asserts that the native handle still exists. The handle is gone, so an `ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION` is thrown from inside stream internals and bypasses the stream's `error` event, the `params()` callback, and the `pipeline()` callback, terminating the process. An application is affected only if it calls `deflate.params()` while streaming to a peer, which is uncommon. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

208.overview: A reachable assertion in Node.js HTTP/2 session teardown lets any unauthenticated client abort the server, over both TLS and cleartext. A client can arrange for an `Http2Stream` that still holds `nghttp2`-allocated header buffers to outlive its session: the stream is removed from the session's stream set but never detached, so when `~Http2Session()` runs the memory accounting is nonzero and the `CHECK_EQ(current_nghttp2_memory_, 0)` assertion fails, terminating the process. The trigger needs only a default `http2` server whose handler responds before the request body has ended, which is typical. It is a variant of CVE-2024-27983 that the earlier fix did not cover, because that fix only detached streams still tracked in the session. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x (since 26.9.0) and 24.x (since 24.22.0).

209.description: HTTPS: a zero-length TLS write re-enters `llhttp_execute()`, and the server copies its own heap into the request body
209.overview: A re-entrancy flaw in Node.js HTTPS lets an unauthenticated client read memory belonging to other connections, including TLS private keys and other users' requests. `TLSWrap::DoWrite()` calls `ClearOut()` directly when asked to write zero bytes; if that write is issued from JavaScript running inside the HTTP parser's `on_body` callback, `ClearOut()` decrypts the next TLS record while the parser is still mid-body, re-entering `llhttp_execute()` and causing a use-after-free and an out-of-bounds heap read. The server then copies that freed or unrelated heap memory into the response for the request body. Triggering it requires a handler that calls `res.flushHeaders()` before the request body ends and later calls `res.end()` with a non-empty chunk, and reading the leaked memory requires any ordinary route that echoes or stores a request body. Cleartext `node:http` is not affected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

210.description: HTTP/2 sessions never clean up if a protocol error is triggered during connection shutdown
210.overview: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can permanently leak Node.js server memory and file descriptors. If a peer triggers a protocol error, for example an oversized frame header, while the session is already shutting down, `nghttp2` tears the session down internally but Node.js never notices, leaving a dangling session: the socket stays in `CLOSE_WAIT` and all of Node.js's HTTP/2 state for that connection is held in memory indefinitely, with no further cost to the attacker. The attacker can start the shutdown remotely by sending `GOAWAY(NO_ERROR)`, so it is reliable against default HTTP/2 servers. It is an incomplete-fix case of CVE-2026-48937: that fix detected `nghttp2` internal terminations by watching for `GOAWAY` sent while not shutting down, but missed terminations that arrive while the session is already shutting down. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

211.description: HTTP/2 stream teardown can send freed response memory to the peer
211.overview: A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 stream teardown can leak response memory, including the contents of other connections' response buffers, to a peer. When a stream is torn down while a write is still backpressured, for example by a peer `RST_STREAM` or by the server's own per-stream timeout destroying the stream, the stream's response buffer is freed but a reference to it is still used, so freed or unrelated heap memory is written to the socket instead of the intended response. On Node.js 26.x and 24.x the teardown can be driven purely by a remote peer once the window-size change from 26.9.0 and 24.22.0 is present, and on all supported lines the same defect is reachable through an application-initiated teardown such as a per-stream idle timeout. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

212.description: CA-only SNI client-CA overrides fail open to the default CA, bypassing per-host mTLS authorization
212.overview: A per-host mutual-TLS authorization bypass in Node.js lets a client authorized for the default hostname reach a protected hostname it is not authorized for. When a TLS server assigns a hostname a different client-certificate CA with `server.addContext(host, { ca: protectedCA })` but no server certificate in that SNI context, the per-host client CA is never installed and the handshake falls back to the default client CA. In `src/crypto/crypto_tls.cc`, `CertCbDone` installs the SNI context's CA only when `setSniContext` succeeds, but `setSniContext` returns `false` for a context with no server certificate, so a CA-only SNI context silently keeps the default CA. A client holding a certificate trusted by the default CA, but not the protected CA, can therefore complete mTLS to the protected hostname and read its response even with `requestCert` and `rejectUnauthorized` enabled, while a client certified by the protected CA is rejected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

213.description: HTTP/2 inbound DATA queued on an undrained stream is charged to no session budget, so maxSessionMemory neither bounds it nor refuses new streams
213.overview: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can exhaust Node.js server memory because inbound DATA queued on an undrained stream is charged to no session budget. Each inbound `DATA` frame creates one JavaScript `Buffer` view in the receiving stream's readable queue, but nothing charges that queue to `current_session_memory_`: the socket read buffer is accounted only during parsing and released immediately, so whatever stays queued is accounted to nothing. A peer that fills a stream's receive window with one-byte `DATA` frames pays about 10 wire bytes per frame while the server retains about 114 bytes per frame, so a single stream on one connection can retain hundreds of megabytes from tens of megabytes sent. `maxSessionMemory` neither bounds the growth nor refuses new streams, because `Http2Session::CanAddStream` gates admission on the same counter that never sees the queue. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

214.description: Proxy credentials disclosed in ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG error messages (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-48615)
214.overview: Node.js discloses proxy credentials in `ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG` error messages. CVE-2026-48615 established that a proxy credential must not appear in a Node.js error message and redacted the username and password from `ProxyConfig.href`, but that fix missed four error paths in the same subsystem, one of them inside the same constructor, which interpolate the raw proxy URL, credentials included, into an `ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG` message. The proxy URL comes from the environment, but the defect is the sink: a secret that Node.js redacts everywhere else is emitted verbatim into a much wider audience than the process environment, such as stderr, container logs, log aggregation, and crash reporting services. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

215.description: Certificate validation bypass in Node.js https.Agent via cross-policy TLS session reuse
215.overview: A certificate validation bypass in Node.js `https.Agent` lets a cached TLS session authenticated under one CA policy be reused by a later request with a stricter policy. `https.Agent.prototype.getName()` assigns the same Agent and session-cache key to a request that omits `ca` and one that explicitly supplies `ca: []`, because an omitted value appends nothing to the key while an empty array stringifies to an empty string. The two policies differ: omitting `ca` uses the default trust store, while supplying `ca` replaces it. Since they share a key, a TLS session authenticated under the broader default policy is handed to a new connection made under the later `ca: []` policy, and TLS 1.3 session resumption carries the earlier authentication forward, so the second request reports `authorized === true` and transmits confidential data to a server its own CA policy would reject on a fresh connection. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

216.description: TLS 1.2 renegotiation allows clients to change servername unilaterally to bypass client certificate authentication
216.overview: A client certificate authentication bypass in Node.js TLS lets a client change the `servername` during TLS 1.2 renegotiation to reach endpoints it was not authorized for. On a server that applies different client-certificate policies per hostname, for example stricter admin-only client-cert auth on one host and ordinary client-cert auth on another, a client that authenticates for a permitted host can renegotiate the TLS 1.2 connection under a different `servername` and carry its existing authentication to the protected host, bypassing the stricter policy. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

217.description: HTTP/2: use-after-free of `Http2Stream` when a `respondWithFile()` stream is reset during a pending write
217.overview: A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client corrupt server memory, over both TLS and cleartext, when the server serves files with `respondWithFile()` or `respondWithFD()`. A client can make the server free an `Http2Stream` while a write request that points to it is still queued on the socket; when that write completes, the code dereferences and makes a virtual call through the freed object. The only precondition is that the application serves a file with `stream.respondWithFile()` or `stream.respondWithFD()`, with default settings otherwise. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x (since 26.9.0) and 24.x (since 24.22.0).

218.description: HTTP/2: cancelling one `respondWithFile()` download crashes the server (NULL dereference in `StreamPipe`)
218.overview: A NULL pointer dereference in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client crash the server, over both TLS and cleartext, by cancelling file downloads. When the server serves a file with `stream.respondWithFile()` or `stream.respondWithFD()` and the client cancels the request, a `StreamPipe` used for the transfer is torn down in an order that leaves a NULL pointer which is then dereferenced, aborting the process. No crafted frames are needed, and a handful of cancelled requests against a default file-serving handler is enough. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

219.description: Remotely triggerable uncaught exception in TLS servers
219.overview: A deferred-callback use-after-destroy in Node.js TLS server handshake handling allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to terminate the server process. When a TLS server uses any of the `SNICallback`, `OCSPRequest`, `newSession`, or `resumeSession` hooks, or `server.addContext()`, the corresponding OpenSSL callbacks are deferred, and the deferred code does not handle the underlying socket being destroyed between scheduling and execution. By sending a client hello that reaches the vulnerable path (for example, no SNI together with an OCSP request) followed by padding and a socket FIN, an attacker makes OpenSSL deliver the client hello and the end-of-file in the same tick, so the socket is destroyed before the deferred callback runs and the process raises an uncaught exception instead of emitting an `'error'` event. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.
